scope: Scoped agent review of ten complete current native viewports: all three terrain atlas pages, two regional material views and five mountain/river views. This records visible findings, not commercial art approval.
observations: All twenty regional surface cards were directly inspected across the three complete atlas pages. Sand ripples, gravel and leaf/grass materials differ, but several forest-floor, meadow and alpine textures still collapse into similar mottled soil at reduced size.

The inspected Yanshan hillshade is smoother within the source-supported land footprint. Thin headwaters have a muted bed and bank halo instead of a single saturated blue stroke. Angular source bends remain visible.
Hankou and Nanjing retain connected main water ribbons and the existing full tactical models. The complete mobile-layout Hankou viewport preserves the same main-channel depiction.

Material/control-area polygon boundaries, detached mountain miniature appearance and crowded near-view models remain visible. These views are not evidence that all terrain or commercial-art issues are resolved.
remaining_visual_issues: Several of the twenty macrogrounds need stronger material-specific shapes, not additional green-brown recolors. Separate Sub2 leaf/needle prototypes are outside this runtime.
Source-supported river and coast geometry remains angular at tactical zoom. Fine banks are cartographic symbols, not historical measurements.
Regional material/control transitions still expose polygons. Mountains need more coherent ridge and foot integration.
Dense near-view units, city-label attachment, full animation coverage and physical Motorola X30 acceptance remain outstanding.
